decisions.reason: The question identifies near-real-time tracking and the one-year Global Carbon Budget lag. The method text supplies the monthly, geographically resolved framing through its reference to global monthly grids.

The poster identifies 10 GOBMs, 8 data products, and Global Carbon Budget 2022. It omits that the historical benchmarks were monthly surface ocean fCO₂ outputs available through December 2021 and that the data products were observation-based.

The poster names convolutional neural networks and semi-supervised learning. It omits the nonlinear relationship to each benchmark’s surface ocean fCO₂ and the combination of supervised prediction error with a consistency loss between weakly and strongly feature-masked inputs.
The poster gives both monthly global variables and the January 2022 through July 2023 period. It omits the 1° × 1° grid resolution and the availability of estimates for each of the 18 benchmarks.
The finding uses µatm for fCO₂ discrepancies. The poster omits the flux-density units, the four inputs to the bulk flux calculation, and the positive-flux direction.

The finding and caption identify the 2020–2021 prediction period and a comparison with the original GOBM average. They omit the 2000–2019 training period, the held-out status of 2020–2021, and the same-month comparison for each original model or product.
The poster omits the fCO₂ correlation analysis and its finding that most benchmark comparisons had R² above 0.9.

The poster reports spatial agreement. It omits the reproduced seasonality of global monthly means for both benchmark groups, the generally positive prediction bias, and the finding that most differences were below 3 µatm.

The poster omits the difficulty predicting extremes, the larger errors in the equatorial Pacific and Arctic, and the reduced accuracy for MPI-SOMFFN associated with frequent historical Arctic data gaps.

notes: The caption identifies Figure 11 as the 10-GOBM average, while the adjacent finding also covers the 8-product average, which has no displayed panel. This is one mismatch in the scope of the displayed evidence. The supplied checklist does not independently verify the under-10 µatm spatial claim. Its under-3 µatm threshold applies to differences in global monthly means, so the omitted result reduces coverage without establishing a numerical error. Section headings and the caption are readable, but the figure’s axes, color scale, and line legend are small. The title, question, method, finding, and caption follow a clear reading order.
